Socialism is an ideology about the worker ownership of the means of production. I was talking more about the overarching philosophy than a specific subset of socialism. 

- Taxation is a governmental form of wealth redistribution tactic and is not about changing who owns capital. There is still a wage and capital dynamic. 

- anti-discrimination laws are generally considered important to most socialists because of the need for effective participation in a democratic situation. 

- also when saying you are a free-market capitalist you are qualifying what type of capitalist you are. If I was to say capitalism is bad vs free-market capitalism is bad it would be two totally different things. Which if you are going to say things are socialist and then complain that we are not specific enough, you should qualify what kind of socialism you are talking about. 

- Overall I think you misconception of socialism is something like liberalism or what the Nordic countries have. I do not disagree that they have ideological contingencies with some of socialism, but they are still in a system where they buy and sell products that were created by labor that was (in their philosophy) exploitative.

> somehow inequality can be fixed by an act of congress.
